title: Through a PRISM, Clearly: Step-Sequence Reasoning for Mistake Recognition in Procedural Videos
abstract: Procedural mistake recognition requires identifying deviations from valid multi-step activities. We study post-completion recognition from videos with benchmark-provided step boundaries. We introduce PRISM (Procedural mistake Recognition via Interpretable Semantic Modeling), which grounds video segments in language and maps their descriptions to procedural states using a lightweight hidden Markov model trained on correct executions. Reference alignment and semantic checks identify errors in step content and order. To support evaluation across heterogeneous benchmarks, we map dataset-specific annotations to four edit-based error types: insertion, deletion, substitution, and transposition. Across three benchmarks, we compare gold and VLM-generated descriptions in raw, semantic-role, and action-object forms. Decoder controls show consistent gains from the trained local decoder over nearest-candidate matching, with additional, dataset-dependent benefits from sequence decoding. Semantic role labeling improves Any-F1 in all six matched grounded comparisons, although the gains vary across datasets and do not translate into uniform improvements under separate configuration selection. These results establish language grounding as an effective interface for explicit procedural mistake reasoning and characterize the contributions of representation and decoding.

title: Developing a Risk-Based Intellectual Property Governance Framework for Generative Artificial Intelligence: A Comparative Analysis of the Eu Ai Act, Uk, and Us Legal Systems
abstract: This paper develops a risk-based intellectual property (IP) governance framework for generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) through doctrinal, comparative, and normative analysis of the European Union (EU), the United Kingdom (UK), and the United States (US). It covers copyright and related IP challenges in data acquisition, model training, output creation, and commercial deployment, as well as the distribution of control, transparency, attribution, and liability in each jurisdiction. The analysis reveals that the EU has several text-and-data-mining exceptions and copyright-policy and training-content-summary obligations for general-purpose AI providers, while the UK has a very limited non-commercial research exception and a unique statutory exception for computer-generated works, and the US is driven primarily by the human-authorship doctrine and fact-specific fair-use analysis. While these strategies offer valuable protections, none alone establish a comprehensive system of organisational control. The study thus suggests an auditing framework linked to the legal basis, data provenance, licenses, human contribution to creativity, output testing, documentation, accountability and escalation, and periodic reassessment, according to the proportionate degree of risk. Rather than harmonizing the three legal systems, the framework sets out a common organizational process for identifying and managing differences in the three legal systems to safeguard the rights holders and to allow for responsible innovation.

title: A Grammar of French Civil Cassation: A Ground-Level Dataset and Tool
abstract: This paper presents a dataset of 121,536 ground-reasons pairs across 86,464 rulings of the five civil chambers of the French Court of Cassation (2016-2025). An appeal on points of law cannot itself be appealed and often decides a case for good. Understanding how the Court rules is thus crucial and can help lawyers who draft those appeals. Inside a ruling, every ground of appeal (a distinct legal complaint against the appealed decision) has its own answer from the Court. This answer is called the reasons and it belongs to one of a few doctrinal families. Using a deterministic pipeline, we pair each ground with its reasons and attach the pair to its family, according to the established French taxonomy. We obtain a descriptive grammar of civil cassation that shows which grounds succeed, which legal texts they refer to, and how both evolve over the decade. We release the dataset, the code and an interactive consultation tool.

title: Positive-unlabelled learning for recorded damp and mould risk in UK housing
abstract: Operational housing records identify damp-and-mould complaints and repairs, while dwellings without recorded events remain unlabelled rather than verified negatives. We formulate recorded damp-and-mould risk prioritisation as a Positive-Unlabelled (PU) learning problem using anonymised UK housing administrative data. The dataset contains 65,214 dwellings described by 291 property-level and household-level snapshot features, with 8,580 recorded positives and 56,634 unlabelled cases. We develop and evaluate a two-stage sample-selection PU framework: an out-of-fold XGBoost scorer first identifies conservative reliable negatives, and weighted Stage-2 classifiers then combine positives, reliable negatives, and weakly weighted residual unlabelled cases. The Stage-1 scorer achieved an out-of-fold development-set PU-AUC of 0.7547. The selected Stage-2 XGBoost model achieved a held-out PU-AUC of 0.7760 and average precision of 0.2981, and increased Recall@20% from 44.0% to 47.0%, retrieving 51 additional recorded positives compared with the Stage-1-only scorer. Supervised XGBoost baselines achieved similar recorded-label performance, while Stage-1 learner ablation showed that the framework supported alternative reliable-negative selectors. Grouped SHAP analysis connected the fitted scores to heating and fuel systems, household and occupancy context, assessment status, dwelling characteristics and energy performance. Targeted predictor exclusion reduced PU-AUC to 0.7648 and Recall@20% to 43.6%, quantifying dependence on selected inputs without resolving their temporal availability. These findings provide an empirical basis for PU-based recorded-risk prioritisation in housing, combining improved ranking over the initial scorer, explicit control over unlabelled training data and interpretation through housing-domain feature groups.

title: What Comes Next and Why: Interpretable Next-Event Prediction with Neuro-Symbolic Rules
abstract: In real-world applications, being able to explain why a prediction is made is often as important - if not more so - than achieving high accuracy. However, existing methods for sequential event prediction typically prioritize accuracy at the expense of interpretability. Neuro-symbolic approaches offer a promising direction to improve interpretability by learning symbolic rules, but extending them to next-event prediction is challenging due to the presence of temporal dependencies. We introduce RULES, a neuro-symbolic model that learns sequential rules directly from data, and combine it with a residual network to form RUNES (Rule Network for Event Sequences). RULES accurately recovers ground truth rules from synthetic data and discovers compact, interpretable rule sets on real data. RUNES combines these rules additively with a residual network, achieving competitive accuracy while providing transparent access to active rules and how residuals adjust predictions.

title: Adaptive MIMO fuzzy PID controller based on Runge-Kutta model
abstract: Nonlinear multi-input multi-output (MIMO) systems are difficult to control because of input–output coupling, measurement noise, and parameter variations. This study proposes a Runge–Kutta (RK) model-based predictive adaptive MIMO fuzzy proportional–integral–derivative (PID) controller for nonlinear dynamical systems. A fourth-order Runge–Kutta (RK4) model predicts future outputs and provides the sensitivity information required to update the fuzzy PID scaling parameters online using the Levenberg–Marquardt (LM) algorithm. An additive correction mechanism provides supplementary control action during transient conditions and plant–model mismatch. Furthermore, a discrete-time Lyapunov-based stability analysis is established, guaranteeing the uniform ultimate boundedness (UUB) of the tracking errors and the boundedness of adaptive parameters under aggregate disturbances. The proposed controller is evaluated on a nonlinear three-tank system under nominal conditions, measurement noise, and time-varying parametric uncertainty. For comparative evaluation, an existing RK model-based adaptive MIMO PID controller is employed as a benchmark under the same operating scenarios. Both controllers maintain bounded tracking responses, control inputs, and adaptive parameters. The composite performance-index values obtained with the proposed fuzzy PID controller are 0.2660, 0.2701, and 1.0739, corresponding to improvements of 6.11%, 6.12%, and 3.59%, respectively, over the benchmark controller. In the parametric-uncertainty case, the RK-based parameter estimator follows the variations in the uncertain inter-tank flow coefficient and reduces the resulting plant–model mismatch. Although the benchmark adaptive PID controller has lower computational requirements, the average and maximum cycle times of both controllers remain substantially below the sampling period. The results demonstrate that the proposed adaptive MIMO fuzzy PID controller improves the combined tracking and control-variation performance while retaining computational feasibility.

title: Can AI Co-Design Structures? An AI Agent for Early-Stage Structural Design
abstract: Recent advances in large language models and agentic workflows offer a new paradigm to early-stage structural design translating design intent into structural models. Although text-to-3D approaches have demonstrated that natural language can be used to produce visual, mesh-based geometric models, structural design requires domain-specific geometric arrangements and semantically rich data types. This paper introduces a proof-of-concept workflow for prompt-to-structure generation using an AI agent connected to a COMPAS-based structural modelling API through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. Through controlled modelling operations, the agent creates and modifies a graph-based structural data model composed of explicit building elements. The resulting artifacts can be inspected, modified, serialised, and further connected to downstream AEC workflows. The approach is demonstrated through selected prompt-to-structure examples and by progressive and editable design sequences that resemble typical iterative structural design workflows. The results are preliminary, but demonstrate the possibility of combining natural language, agentic workflows, and domain-specific structural data structures as a first step toward AI-assisted structural co-design.

title: Where Do Long Captions Fail? Position-Aware Diagnosis and Reinforcement Learning for Detailed Image Captioning
abstract: Detailed image captioning is usually framed as an amount problem: a model should mention more visual facts while avoiding hallucination. However, autoregressive VLMs generate captions as ordered sequences, and later generations may be produced under weaker or noisier visual grounding. We therefore argue that long-form captioning should be studied not only by what facts are mentioned, but also by where they appear. We introduce a position-aware rubric representation that decomposes dense human references into atomic visual claims, verifies generated captions against those claims, and induces a quartile-wise composition of supported, hallucinated, and generic content. This lens reveals two qualitatively different failures in long captions: models tend to produce unsupported specificity in the middle, while the final portion often escapes into vague, non-evidential language rather than simply accumulating more hallucination. A same-reference human control does not exhibit these patterns; additional human audits examine the visual validity of the induced labels. Motivated by this diagnosis, we propose PAGER (Position-Aware Grounded Evidence Reinforcement), a GRPO training objective with separate signals for supported fine-grained middle evidence, evidence-bearing tail continuation, claim coverage, and content-aware length control. The result is a closed loop: the same ordered claim representation identifies where long captions fail and supplies the position-specific reward needed to repair those failures. Experiments on detailed-caption benchmarks show that PAGER improves position-wise grounding and pairwise caption preference while preserving competitive global caption quality.

title: SAFAR-Onto: A Halal Tourism Ontology Developed Through Hybrid AI–Human Engineering
abstract: Halal tourism is a fast-growing market. However, information about halal services, certifications, and facilities is scattered across many sources. Existing tourism ontologies model general tourism concepts such as destinations, activities, and accommodations, but they do not represent Islamic requirements such as prayer facilities, halal certification, or dietary compliance. Manual ontology development is slow. Large language models (LLMs) can speed up concept extraction and hierarchy proposal, but they cannot decide religious or cultural matters. In this article, we present SAFAR-Onto, an OWL 2 DL ontology for halal tourism. We develop it through a hybrid AI–human process across four phases: knowledge acquisition, conceptualization, formalization, and dual validation. The process adapts METHONTOLOGY and Simple Knowledge Engineering. LLMs assist with concept extraction and dimensional analysis. An Islamic studies validation gate routes culturally sensitive decisions to human experts. We evaluate the ontology with two methods: expert review across five quality dimensions, and the OQuaRE technical metrics. SAFAR-Onto contains 10 main classes, 75 subclasses, 201 object properties, and 200 data properties, built from 67 validated domain concepts. Six experts from tourism management, computer science, and Islamic studies rated the ontology between 4.0 and 4.5 on a five-point Likert scale, with accuracy highest at 4.5. Fourteen of 18 OQuaRE metrics scored Excellent or Very Good. We also report a verified mapping from expert feedback to ontology revisions. The ontology is publicly available at https://w3id.org/def/SAFAROnto under a CC-BY-4.0 license. We hypothesize that the development process can transfer to adjacent culturally specific domains such as Islamic finance and kosher food systems.

We evaluate the ontology with two methods: expert review across five quality dimensions, and the OQuaRE technical metrics. SAFAR-Onto contains 10 main classes, 75 subclasses, 201 object properties, and 200 data properties, built from 67 validated domain concepts. Six experts from tourism management, computer science, and Islamic studies rated the ontology between 4.0 and 4.5 on a five-point Likert scale, with accuracy highest at 4.5. Fourteen of 18 OQuaRE metrics scored Excellent or Very Good. We also report a verified mapping from expert feedback to ontology revisions. The ontology is publicly available at https://w3id.org/def/SAFAROnto under a CC-BY-4.0 license. We hypothesize that the development process can transfer to adjacent culturally specific domains such as Islamic finance and kosher food systems.

title: DRAFT: Decoding and Reconstructing 3D Room Layouts from fMRI and Camera Trajectories
abstract: While functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) decoders reconstruct images and 3D objects, recovering the metric geometry of rooms from a moving viewpoint remains an open challenge. We introduce, to our knowledge for the first time, the task of reconstructing 3D layouts of held-out scenes using only the known camera trajectories and the fMRI signals of participants watching indoor walkthroughs, without any visual frames. The task is hard because of the temporal mismatch between rapid visual changes and blurred fMRI signals. Our method, DRAFT (Decoding and Reconstructing 3D room lAyouts from fMRI and Trajectories), extracts a compact layout representation from the early visual cortex and fuses this neural code with the geometric free space derived from camera motion. To evaluate it, we propose layout r, the Pearson correlation between predicted and ray-cast log depths. On ten held-out scenes (20 participants), DRAFT reaches a layout r of 0.480, outperforming the camera path alone (0.446) and seven fMRI decoders (at most 0.429). DRAFT also works as a plug-in that improves all seven decoders without retraining, raising their layout r from 0.171-0.429 to 0.487-0.493. Brain activity and camera motion can thus recover the metric layout of unseen rooms, a first step toward reconstructing the 3D spaces people see.

title: PIU Smart Intelligence Agents: Design and Implementation of a Security-Aware Multi-Agent Architecture for Enterprise Intelligence
abstract: Enterprises increasingly rely on heterogeneous documents, relational databases, and analytical systems to support information retrieval and business decision-making. Integrating large language models (LLMs) with these sources introduces challenges in evidence reliability, analytical correctness, access control, and operational resilience. This paper presents PIU Smart Intelligence Agents, a security-aware multi-agent architecture designed to integrate enterprise document intelligence, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), semantic search, document summarization, naturallanguage-to-SQL analytics, key performance indicator (KPI) generation, and conversational AI within a common application and governance framework. The proposed architecture organizes specialized AI capabilities around shared services for authentication, authorization, request validation, provider integration, observability, and controlled data access. Its document-processing workflow encompasses file validation, text extraction, optical character recognition for scanned documents, normalization, chunking, embedding generation, and vector-based indexing. The structured-analytics workflow separates schema-aware query generation from SQL validation, restricted database execution, and result interpretation. The architecture also addresses provider compatibility, timeout handling, failure recovery, document lifecycle management, and traceability of generated outputs. The source implementation reports 1,242 automated tests passed and two integration tests skipped. These results are reported implementation evidence and have not been independently reproduced. The available evidence does not establish comprehensive external RAG benchmark performance, quantitative correctness across all agents, independently validated security effectiveness, or production-scale performance and recovery guarantees. Accordingly, this study presents an integrated engineering architecture and identifies a reproducible evaluation framework for assessing its effectiveness. The principal contribution is the systematic integration of heterogeneous enterprise AI capabilities with explicit governance and validation requirements, rather than the introduction of a new learning or retrieval algorithm. Future work should prioritize agent-specific correctness testing, retrieval and answer-quality benchmarks, adversarial security evaluation, controlled load testing, and recovery verification.

title: Learning What to Ask for Tomorrow: Active Preference Acquisition for Long-Term Personalized Web Agents
abstract: Web agents increasingly serve the same user across repeated online tasks such as booking travel, shopping, and scheduling, so their long-term usefulness depends on how well they know the user's preferences. Passive memory and personalization methods cannot obtain preferences the user never reveals, and clarification methods that value a question by its benefit to the current task overlook the benefit of reusing the answer in later tasks. We study Active Preference Acquisition (APA): which missing preferences are worth the cost of asking? We define the Prospective Personalization Value (PPV) of a missing preference as its expected cumulative utility gain over future tasks minus the effort and disclosure-risk cost of asking, and select questions under a per-interaction budget. We characterize when cumulative reuse justifies acquisition despite insufficient single-task benefit, and evaluate this regime with an initial-profile diagnostic. APA computes the counterfactual gain of each candidate preference on public task prototypes with the agent's own task solver and aggregates it by the expected reuse of each task family. We evaluate it on ActiveWebPref, a controlled longitudinal benchmark with hidden but queryable user profiles and exact task utilities. At a horizon of 20 tasks, 34.4% of budget-feasible valuable missing preferences are amortization-dependent; APA acquires 80.3% of them, whereas current-task value of information acquires 5.1%. Under per-user asking-cost caps matched to APA's realized expenditure, APA achieves higher net utility than four heuristic selection baselines. In our cost setting, asking about every unknown preference yields lower net utility than not asking, while APA recovers 84.2% of its utility gain with 27.6% of its questions. The value of acquiring a user preference should account for its reuse across future tasks, not only its benefit to the task at hand.

title: Computational Text Mining Framework for Indonesian Economic Diplomacy Corpus
abstract: This study presents a computational communication framework for analyzing framing and public sentiment in Indonesian digital media discourse about economic agreements between the Republic of Indonesia (RI) and the United States of America (US). Employing a corpus of 4,217 Twitter posts and digital news items collected from 15 February 2026 to 25 February 2026, the study applies text pre-processing, lexicon-based sentiment labeling (InSet and VADER), TF-IDF and Word2Vec feature extraction, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification. Results indicate that an SVM classifier trained on InSet-generated labels achieves 72% agreement with those labels, exceeding a VADER-labeled counterpart (64%). Over this ten-day observation window, lexicon-derived sentiment skewed predominantly negative (40.8% under InSet), dominated by economic-frame vocabulary centered on trade, tariffs, and investment. The study contributes a replicable Data Science pipeline for public-diplomacy communication research in non-English-language contexts, bridging computational linguistics, communication theory, and international relations scholarship.

title: Who Is the Influencer? Consensus Dynamics in Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems are increasingly used in practice, but their behavior is complex and hard to understand. We design a simple task to ask which model has the most influence on the final consensus when several models are mixed in one system. Experimentally, across seven model families, we find that the opinions of the other models are absorbed into the opinion of the stronger model, the one with more parameters. This happens even though the task requires no pretraining knowledge and has no correct answer. To understand this phenomenon, we interpret the agents as weighted particles moving on a simplex. Larger models carry a larger weight and therefore occupy a deeper well in the energy landscape. A large weight means strong in-context learning: a model with a large weight amplifies the majority of its context. Larger models are generally better at in-context learning, and this is what makes the larger model the influencer. We hope that this work helps to interpret multi-agent systems, whose behavior is becoming too complex for humans to understand.

title: DeepOpen: Decision-Oriented Intent Classification on BANKING77 and CLINC150
abstract: We present DeepOpen, a decision-Oriented intent-classification framework with dataset- specific systems for BANKING77 and CLINC150. On BANKING77, a single English classi- fier continued with sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) achieves 94.1234% test accuracy (2,899/3,080). This is the best observed result among three fixed SAM seeds, selected for display after test evaluation; their mean is 94.0368%. On the 150 in-scope CLINC150 classes, probability fusion of one Laya specialist and three DeBERTa-v3-large classifiers achieves 98.0222% (4,411/4,500). We describe the two configurations, reproduce the reference com- parisons displayed in the accompanying evaluation explorer, and separate headline scores from evidence about improvement. Under a uniform BANKING77 evaluation path, the SAM mean exceeds the historical checkpoint by 0.0433 percentage points, with a shared-row 95% interval of [-0.2273, +0.3247]. Thus, the continuation does not establish a reliable accuracy gain. The report documents strong observed task-specific performance, selection effects, and unresolved historical execution-path differences, rather than a new backbone or a unified algorithmic advantage.

title: PENERAPAN METODE EXTREME LEARNING MACHINE UNTUK MENINGKATKAN AKURASI ALGORITMA K-NEAREST NEIGHBORS DALAM KLASIFIKASI PENYAKIT KANKER PAYUDARA
abstract: Breast cancer is a major health concern that poses a significant threat to women across the globe. While early detection plays a vital role in improving survival rates, achieving high diagnostic accuracy continues to be a challenge. In this study, the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm is employed as a fundamental classification technique, which is further enhanced using the Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) to boost the accuracy of breast cancer classification. The dataset utilized in this research was obtained from Kaggle, comprising 569 samples with 32 features. The research methodology involves data preprocessing, dividing the dataset into training and testing sets with different ratios, and assessing the model’s performance through a confusion matrix.The results show that integrating ELM into KNN increases the average accuracy from 70.86% to 95.44%, achieving the highest accuracy of 96.50% at a 75% training and 25% testing ratio. These findings confirm that the ELM–KNN combination produces a more accurate and efficient model for breast cancer diagnosis.

title: Solving Flood-It Puzzles: A Comparison of Tailored A* Search with Declarative Solver Approaches
abstract: We present an optimized approach for finding minimal move sequences to solve Flood-It puzzles using A* search and compare it with approaches using SAT, Integer Programming, and Constraint Programming solvers. The performance of A* search is considerably improved by using an appropriate heuristic and sophisticated equivalences of game states to limit the search space. Each aspect is systematically evaluated, providing insights that generalize to other problems. By comparing the best variant of each approach, the A* search is the fastest in finding a minimal solution in about 75 % of the Flood-It instances tested. This result is in line with our expectation since A* specifically looks for a minimum solution. In contrast, the SAT-based approach is designed to solve the decision problem of whether a solution with a given length exists. An iterative search is required to determine a minimum solution length using a SAT-based approach. However, with increasing complexity, quantified by the minimum solution length, the SAT-based approach outperforms A*. We also compared the different approaches to the decision problem, where A* again performed best for the largest number of puzzles. Here, again, SAT supersedes A* for higher complexities, albeit with a lower crossing point.

title: RIFT: KV Cache Compression for Draft Models with Complementary Compressibility Training
abstract: Speculative decoding is a popular decode acceleration method. As such, it is particularly relevant to long-output generation, which requires an increasingly large KV cache. KV cache compression offers a way to constrain costs in long-context drafting. However, compression methods that focus on prefill information can lose relevance as the output length grows. We term this phenomenon decode staleness and show that it degrades draft model accuracy under selection-based KV cache compression. We introduce RIFT, a family of selection-based KV cache compression strategies that balance prefill information and recent generated tokens. We show that refreshing the KV cache selection during token generation significantly improves the drafter's quality at the cost of additional decode latency. To alleviate the refresh costs, we propose an adaptive KV refresh strategy that reduces the number of score calculations while retaining the drafter's quality. We further demonstrate how a compressibility-driven drafter training phase, based on sparse attention masks, can improve the drafter's quality under a compressed KV cache. Combined with compressibility training, RIFT enables Qwen3.5-4B, drafting for Qwen3.5-122B, to retain over 98% of its full-cache acceptance length on 32K-token inputs, 4K-token outputs, and an 8K-token KV cache budget.

title: Co-Recursive Semantic Self-Extension: A Mathematical Foundation for Open-Ended Intelligence
abstract: Artificial intelligence has advanced through scale, data, and computation, yet remains bounded by its representational framework. We ask what makes intelligence open-ended. Every inferential system selects meaningful distinctions, limiting what it can learn. Within a fixed purpose, performance reaches a ceiling set by its semantic domain. Teleological succession, in which purposes arise from earlier ones, faces a similar limit: Boolean-closed purpose-transformations exhaust their reachable semantic territory. We shift from purposes to inferential systems. Drawing on Kant and Gödel, we model cognitive states as partial evaluations over a formal language. Unresolved propositions may be undecided or undecidable. Reasoning can resolve the former but not the latter, leaving a frontier for extension. Non-trivial reductions of undecidable propositions expose undecidable intermediate premises whose reflective reification supports multiple decisive extensions. Finite trace-guided generation remains fallible, requiring meta-level selection and polycontextural exploration. Using Kolmogorov complexity, we show that no architecture with a fixed state description, transition mechanism, and initial condition can generate histories incorporating irreducible algorithmic information. Because physical systems are fixed in this sense, we examine collectives. Coupling finitely many finite agents does not remove the bound. Extension requires persistent external memory preserving semantic content and historical coordinates. Collective generative capacity depends on balancing overlap for transfer with difference for generation. We propose semantic self-extension as a design principle: intelligence should not merely resolve ambiguity within existing meanings, but transform unresolved structures into new spaces of meaning, generating new distinctions, questions, representations, and purposes.

title: What Pairwise Evaluation Misses: Reward Scores across Prompts
abstract: Reward models score responses for preference optimization, filtering and ranking, and pooling scores across prompts needs them to be comparable. Yet pairwise evaluation compares two responses to the same prompt, so any score component shared by a prompt's responses cancels and goes untested. We study this component by comparing between-prompt variation in model scores with the same variation in human ratings of the same responses. We propose a human-referenced audit, built from a between-prompt variance share, a sibling-rating regression and prompt substitutions, and apply it to eighteen released scorers and six matched training conditions. We find that scores cluster by prompt more than the ratings do: on HelpSteer2, six reward models have between-prompt shares of 0.34 to 0.64 against a human share near zero. Replacing the original prompt with a fixed instruction keeps substantial clustering but weakens agreement with prompt-level human ratings, so clustering alone does not show agreement with humans. Part of that variation is useful: subtracting prompt means lowers the helpfulness of globally selected responses, and scores stay sensitive to a wrong prompt even when training shuffles prompt means. We propose that reward evaluation check between-prompt variation, sensitivity to a wrong prompt and usefulness for selection separately.

title: Transformers with CoT Discover Heavy-Ball Acceleration Through Training
abstract: Modern transformers often solve complex tasks by generating and refining intermediate reasoning steps. To develop a theoretical understanding of chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, a notable recent study by Huang et al. (2025) viewed transformers as algorithm executors, and showed that when transformers' CoT steps are supervised by a gradient-descent teacher, they can learn to implement gradient descent for in-context weight prediction in linear regression. In this paper, we study the same in-context weight prediction task but ask whether CoT reasoning can go beyond merely imitating the teacher algorithm. We show that, after initial supervision from a gradient-descent teacher, further trajectory-level supervision using the true regression weights leads the model to implement the Heavy-Ball method, thereby achieving acceleration over the original teacher. Notably, this accelerated algorithm emerges without supervision from any Heavy-Ball teacher. Our results provide a concrete theoretical example in which transformer reasoning can discover new algorithms through training, rather than merely imitate the algorithm used for supervision.

title: The Role of AI in Virtual Experimentation and Modeling
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a potentially life-altering technology in virtual experimentation and modeling, and has led to increased simulation precision, decreased processing time and enhanced decision-making within the industrial or education sector. This chapter discusses the role of AI algorithms, in particular, machine learning and deep learning, in being adopted in the context of digital twins, computational models and virtual labs. The use of AI makes it possible to execute iterations of the experimental setting quickly, and scientists can simulate several situations and parameters without the limitations inherent in actual experimentation. Classical simulation approaches often require extensive manual calibration and are sensitive to parameterized models, making it difficult to account for real-world variability. Deep learning neural networks and physics-based simulation models are used within the hybrid modeling methodology.

title: I$^2$-KAN: Interpretable Intra- and Inter-Modal Multi-Pathway Representation Learning for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) aims to infer sentiment by integrating linguistic, acoustic, and visual information. However, many fusion methods integrate modality-specific representations and cross-modal interactions into joint representations, making it difficult to determine whether predictive utility arises from a modality itself or from its interactions with others. More fundamentally, a modality's standalone predictive utility may not faithfully reflect its interaction-conditioned predictive utility. To address this issue, we propose I$^2$-KAN, an interpretable multi-pathway framework that explicitly maintains intra-modal and pairwise inter-modal information in separate structural pathways. Each pathway is refined by a Task-Decoupled Linear-Gated Denoising Bottleneck (TDL-GDB) to learn compact and task-relevant representations, followed by structured Kolmogorov-Arnold Network fusion that retains explicit pathway associations and supports multi-level interpretation. Extensive experiments on CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, and CH-SIMS v2 demonstrate strong overall performance. Ablation and interpretability analyses consistently show across the three benchmarks that low standalone predictive utility does not necessarily imply low interaction-conditioned predictive utility: a modality that appears weak in isolation can remain informative through pairwise interactions. These findings highlight the interaction-dependent nature of multimodal utility and suggest that modality utility should be characterized from both standalone and interaction-conditioned perspectives.

title: INTEGRASE K-MEANS, LATENT DIRICHLET ALLOCATION, DAN ANALISIS SENTIMEN UNTUK ANALISIS MULTIDIMENSI UMPAN BALIK MAHASISWA
abstract: This study aims to cluster student feedback on lecturers in the Academic Information System (SIAKAD) of Universitas PGRI Kanjuruhan Malang using the K-Means algorithm. We analyzed 33,229 comments through text preprocessing stages (normalization, tokenization, stopword removal, and stemming). Subsequently, we transformed the comments into numerical representations using the Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) method. We determined the optimal cluster number via the Elbow method, yielding three clusters. Evaluation of cluster quality using the Silhouette Score revealed a relatively low value (0.084). Nevertheless, further analysis with Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and lexicon-based sentiment analysis uncovered unique characteristics for each cluster: (1) dominated by general appreciation (good, friendly), (2) focused on learning aspects (clear material, teaching methods), and (3) containing personal comments and specific criticisms (excessive assignments, slow grading). These findings demonstrate that comment clustering complemented by topic modeling and sentiment analysis can provide strategic insights for the university to support academic decision-making (e.g., lecturer development programs) and enhance teaching quality in a targeted manner.

title: MQAScore: Fine-Grained Text-Music Alignment Evaluation via Large Audio Language Model
abstract: Text-to-music alignment is commonly evaluated by the global similarity between text and audio embeddings, which collapses all described attributes into a single score and obscures which ones are missing. We instead introduce MQAScore, which verifies each atomic musical concept along five clip-level dimensions (genre, instrument, mood/theme, vocal, and usage) by the probability that a large audio language model (LALM) answers affirmatively to a binary question. To assess evaluator reliability, we construct verification labels from presence/absence annotations and LLM-guided concept substitutions, and propose the Sensitivity-Invariance Ratio, which measures how selectively an evaluator responds to meaning-changing substitutions. Experiments show that concept-level scoring improves both question-answering and similarity-based evaluators, and MQAScore can be a more reliable and interpretable fine-grained complement to global similarity for evaluating text-to-music alignment.

title: Enterprise Agentic RAG with Pre-Search Role-Based Access Control, Multi-Layered Guardrails, and Operational Telemetry
abstract: While Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) significantly enhances the factual accuracy of Large Language Models (LLMs), standard implementations face critical enterprise vulnerabilities including vector embedding side-channel leakage, unauthorized privilege escalation, prompt injection susceptibility, unmonitored autonomous execution, and lack of regulatory observability. This paper introduces Enterprise Agentic RAG, an innovative production-grade architecture combining a stateful 7-agent orchestration workflow (LangGraph) with strict Pre-Search Vector Payload Filtering across four security clearance tiers (Restricted, Confidential, Internal, and Public). The proposed system integrates hybrid retrieval combining BM25 lexical scoring with dense vector cosine similarity (Qdrant HNSW indexing) optimized through Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). Furthermore, the pipeline features an autonomous Tool Agent capable of policy-validated, AES-256 encrypted corporate email dispatch, an egress Data Loss Prevention (DLP) firewall preventing unauthorized data exfiltration, deterministic multi-layered guardrails neutralizing adversarial prompt injections, jailbreaks, PII exposures, and sensitive credential leaks, alongside real-time Prometheus operational telemetry and an immutable audit logging engine. Empirical benchmarking demonstrates 100% RBAC pre-filter precision, zero vector embedding leakage across privilege boundaries, 98.7% average groundedness score, sub-150ms end-to-end orchestration latency, and 100% interception of adversarial injection and DLP egress violations, establishing an enterprise-ready framework for secure corporate intelligence synthesis.

title: nnInteractive Agent: General-Purpose AI Agents as 3D Image Annotators
abstract: Interactive 3D segmentation models such as nnInteractive turn a few spatial prompts (points, scribbles, boxes) into accurate volumetric masks, but a human still does the annotation work: finding each structure, placing prompts, checking the result and correcting it. General-purpose AI agents can now interpret images, call tools and write code. We show that such agents can take over this work without additional training: the user makes a request in plain language, and the agent works out what has to be segmented, locates the targets, prompts nnInteractive, inspects the 3D result, corrects it and responds to feedback. Asked for 'the muscles used for chewing', an agent identifies and segments the masseters and pterygoids; asked to count liver lesions, it writes its own code to find candidates and splits a merged lesion on request. Our open-source nninteractive-agent provides nnInteractive as tools over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), together with a skill that encodes how experienced users prompt it. On a benchmark spanning CT, MRI, PET and micro-CT of humans, a mouse and an ant (14 images; 51 targets from organs and tumours to muscles, foot bones, vessel trees and an insect brain), Claude Code and Codex reach a mean Dice of 0.81 and 0.84 from the request alone; when told where each target is, both reach 0.85 and prompt nearly as effectively as an oracle that places prompts using the reference segmentation. A text-prompted 3D model (VoxTell) is more accurate on most standard radiological targets but less robust: it returns an empty mask for one of them and fails on the leg muscles, the foot bones, the mouse and the ant, where the agents remain accurate. Code: https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nninteractive-agent

title: Cyber Defence, Agentic AI, and the Sociotechnical Paradigm: A Survey of AI-Driven Cybersecurity
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) are reshaping cybersecurity, moving it from signature-based reactive security to agentic, self-evolving, and proactive operations. However, the fast deployment of autonomous agents entails significant security issues, physical-layer attacks in cyber-physical systems, alignment problems, and advanced social engineering risks jeopardizing the stability of the modern sociotechnical infrastructures. This survey paper, which summarizes and analyses the literature, examines the duality of AI in cybersecurity, exploring its implications for strengthening digital defences and increasing the threat landscape for adversaries. We perform a thorough review of 36 cutting-edge research articles, which are organized into six important areas: self-evolving defensive paradigms, LLM-based intelligent agents, reinforcement learning for autonomous decision-making, security of cyber-physical systems, human-machine co-teaming, and agent alignment. Our synthesis shows that multi-agent collaborations greatly shorten incident response times and automate discovery of vulnerabilities but are also highly vulnerable to prompt injection, training data poisoning, and physical-layer spoofing. Moreover, we identify a shift from model patches to model alignment and constitutional safety at runtime as a prerequisite for securing these systems. We believe that resilient digital defence must also be considered a sociotechnical problem, as there must be agents, autonomous systems, that are governed by other agents, aligned and constitutionally bound, and are able to collaborate, rather than operate completely separately, with human operators.

title: When Forgotten Facts Return: Relearning-Aware Unlearning of Knowledge Graph Embeddings via Tangent Kernels
abstract: Approximate unlearning answers a deletion request on a knowledge-graph embedding by editing entity embeddings instead of retraining from scratch. These embeddings keep being updated as new facts arrive. Under this ordinary continued training, forgotten facts recover more than in the exact-unlearning baseline, a model retrained without them and given the same continued training. We trace this relearning to entity embeddings shared by forgotten and new facts. To our knowledge, this is the first study of relearning in knowledge-graph embeddings. Relearning-robust methods developed for deep networks do not account for the graph structure underlying this recovery. We propose Kernel-Anticipated Unlearning (KAU), which uses the tangent kernel to model how continued training changes forgotten facts' scores through these shared parameters. KAU expresses this first-order response in closed form and differentiates through it inside the forgetting loss. The objective steers edits toward directions that continued training reverses less. We compare KAU with state-of-the-art knowledge-graph unlearners and relearning-robust methods under identical continued training, measuring leakage beyond the exact-unlearning baseline. Across three backbones, KAU reduces the strongest knowledge-graph unlearner's leakage by 46-63% on FB15k-237 and 50-82% on CoDEx-L, at higher retained utility.

title: Federated Differentially Private Optimization via Low-Rank Preconditioning
abstract: We consider differentially private (DP) optimization in the federated setting, where a DP estimate of the feature covariance matrix serves as a Hessian approximation for generalized linear models. Existing central DP methods for covariance estimation have communication cost that grows quadratically in the data dimension, while existing baselines with linear communication cost are only locally private and degrade as the number of clients increases. As a remedy, we propose a federated DP-PCA framework that achieves linear communication cost while providing central DP guarantees under secure aggregation. It consists of a DP rank selection step, a DP power method, and a noisy release of the covariance projected onto the selected low-dimensional subspace. We give error bounds for this covariance estimate and for the resulting low-communication preconditioned DP gradient descent. Empirically, our proposed DP optimization method matches a centralized baseline with quadratic communication cost at a fraction of the communication.

title: Dialect-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Arabic Question Answering: Measuring and Mitigating the Moroccan Darija–MSA Retrieval Gap
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems for Arabic are evaluated almost exclusively with Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) queries, although users write in dialect. We study this mismatch with a parallel benchmark of 200 questions written in both MSA and Moroccan Darija over 3,054 Arabic Wikipedia passages. Dialectal queries lower hybrid-retrieval Recall@1 from 0.755 to 0.620, and the loss reaches the answers: with five retrieved passages, answer correctness falls from 0.810 to 0.690, mostly through additional refusals; part of this loss persists even when the gold passage is supplied directly, so retrieval is the larger but not the only component. Rewriting Darija queries into MSA does not help. Zero-shot cross-encoder reranking raises dialectal Recall@1 to 0.800 (MSA: 0.755 unreranked, 0.875 reranked) and lets a single retrieved passage replace five unreranked passages with no loss larger than five percentage points and a 3.7-fold shorter prompt. Because dialectal queries are retrieved with lower confidence, gating the reranker on the retriever’s score margin concentrates its cost on them without any dialect detection, retaining 94% of the benefit while reranking about half of the queries. The findings hold under a human-validated LLM judge (Cohen’s κ=0.797), Holm correction and three prompt wordings, and replicate judge-free on a second, Darija-trained generator. We release the benchmark, corpus, code and all result files.

title: Dual Exam: Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Agents and World Models
abstract: World Models (WMs) can support Multimodal Agents (MAs) through simulated experience, while Agent trajectories can inform World Model refinement. Evaluating this interaction requires separate evidence about action selection and state evolution. We introduce Dual Exam, which tests Agents under fixed environment response mechanisms and World Models under fixed action interventions across physical, digital, social, and scientific domains. The Agent track compares 10 configurations on 1,088 items in 15 reporting categories. The World Model track contains 400 cases across eight scenarios; 15 configurations have full coverage and one covers six scenarios. GPT 6 Astra leads the case-weighted Agent Index at 31.3, and GPT-Image-2 leads the full-coverage WM Overall at 21.7. These scores use different tasks and metrics and are not directly comparable. A 150-case pilot of one coupled pairing records zero task successes and motivates component-level diagnosis. Results reveal uneven task performance and failures to preserve task-relevant state. Their value for predicting coupled success or sustained reciprocal learning remains to be established.

title: A General-Purpose Dual-Path Interaction Framework for Multi-View Medical Image Segmentation: Alleviating Data Volume Dependency in Small-Sample Regimes
abstract: The performance of medical image segmentation depends on a large amount of annotated data, and most segmentation models experience a significant drop in performance in low-sample-size scenarios. Existing semi-supervised and weakly supervised methods rely on specific network architectures, while traditional multi-view-assisted segmentation methods require strictly paired samples, which limits their clinical applications. To address these issues, we propose DPIF, a general-purpose plug-and-play dual-path interaction framework compatible with arbitrary encoder-decoder segmentation networks, which leverages cross-view anatomical complementarity to reduce annotation reliance. DPIF first performs Sinkhorn optimal transport-based cross-view distribution alignment to establish global semantic correspondence without sample-level pairing. It then adopts conditional mutual information-guided feature decoupling to enable bidirectional knowledge transfer only within the shared semantic space, suppressing view-specific noise. Finally, persistent homology-based topological regularization encodes anatomical invariants as unsupervised priors to mitigate overfitting. Experiments were conducted using 24 baseline models on a private multicenter echocardiography dataset and two public datasets. The results show that DPIF-enhanced models outperform single-view baseline models when trained on comparable amounts of data. Notably, most dual-path variants trained on 40\% - 60\% of the data achieve performance comparable to that of single-view models trained on the full dataset. This demonstrates that DPIF provides a general-purpose and scalable solution for data-scarce multi-view medical image segmentation problems.

title: An Explainable Attention‐Driven EfficientNetB7 Framework for Early Detection of Head and Neck Cancer Using Digital Holographic Microscopy
abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents a deep learning (DL) framework for head and neck cancer (HNC) detection using holographic imaging data. A self‐curated dataset of holographic and corresponding bright‐field images is used for comparative evaluation, demonstrating the novelty of the approach. The framework employs an EfficientNetB7 backbone integrated with a convolutional block attention module (CBAM) to enhance feature representation via channel and spatial attention mechanisms. To address class imbalance, class weighting and focal loss are applied to improve learning for minority classes. Experimental results demonstrated strong performance, achieving 96.93% validation accuracy, 97.80% test accuracy, and 99.31% area under the curve (AUC), outperforming bright‐field imaging data. The attention‐guided model improved classification performance by up to 12.72% over baseline models. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for accurate and early detection of HNC. Furthermore, explainability is incorporated using gradient‐weighted class activation mapping (Grad‐CAM) variants and local interpretable model‐agnostic explanations (LIME), providing qualitative visual insights into the model's decision‐making process, thereby facilitating its potential use in future computer‐aided decision support.

The framework employs an EfficientNetB7 backbone integrated with a convolutional block attention module (CBAM) to enhance feature representation via channel and spatial attention mechanisms. To address class imbalance, class weighting and focal loss are applied to improve learning for minority classes. Experimental results demonstrated strong performance, achieving 96.93% validation accuracy, 97.80% test accuracy, and 99.31% area under the curve (AUC), outperforming bright‐field imaging data. The attention‐guided model improved classification performance by up to 12.72% over baseline models. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for accurate and early detection of HNC. Furthermore, explainability is incorporated using gradient‐weighted class activation mapping (Grad‐CAM) variants and local interpretable model‐agnostic explanations (LIME), providing qualitative visual insights into the model's decision‐making process, thereby facilitating its potential use in future computer‐aided decision support.

title: SCOPE: Compiling Natural-Language Policies into Neurosymbolic Predicate Programs
abstract: Policy enforcement for LLM agents has shifted from single-turn content moderation to compound, application-specific policies evaluated over multi-turn transcripts and tool-call trajectories. Fine-tuned guardrail models are efficient but degrade on compound policies, and while LLM-as-a-judge approaches achieve higher accuracy, they incur high inference cost and tend to produce unstable predictions. Neurosymbolic methods offer a natural alternative, decomposing the policy into narrow neural decisions composed under explicit logic. However, existing symbolic layers lack the required expressiveness and are optimized against fixed data rather than the policy itself. To address this, we introduce SCOPE, which compiles a policy into an executable program of neural predicates executed by small models, deterministic extractors, and code that composes their outputs. The program is optimized jointly with its training data, using adversarial generation of counterexamples that target where the program deviates from the policy. We evaluate SCOPE on a benchmark of real-world policy tasks against prompt optimization, task decomposition, and workflow generation methods, achieving the highest average accuracy across tasks and models. Programs optimized with the weakest executor transfer to other models without further optimization. This allows them to be deployed in production on inexpensive models, where they reach accuracy comparable to frontier reasoning models. Unlike these monolithic models, SCOPE produces substantially more stable predictions, and each verdict is interpretable through the predicate outputs that produced it. Additionally, we validate the key components of our method through an ablation study. SCOPE thus enables reliable, interpretable, and efficient policy enforcement at production scale.

title: A multi-task learning approach for consumer sentiment classification and emotion detection via behavioral data
abstract: Sentiment analysis captures overall opinion polarity, but it often fails to reveal the key emotions that drive consumer behavior. The recognition of both sentiment and emotions provides crucial information to uncover underlying drivers of consumers behavior and brand loyalty. These important insights enable businesses to detect emerging issues, refine products and services, and personalize consumer experiences. This study proposes a multi-task approach that performs sentiment classification and emotion detection tasks based on consumer reviews and corresponding ratings. To this end, we propose Consumer Sentiment and Emotion Modeling ( COSMO-MT ), a deep learning-based multi-task model for sentiment classification and emotion detection. It begins with an input layer followed by embedding layers that provide sentiment-specific, emotion-specific, and shared embeddings from the input text. Each embedding is processed through shared layers consisting of CNN, BiLSTM, and attention mechanisms. Moreover, several auxiliary features are incorporated into the shared layers to provide explicit linguistic information. The outputs of the shared layers are then passed to task-specific layers for sentiment classification and emotion detection. Finally, corresponding dense and output layers generate predictions for both tasks. We evaluate the efficacy of the proposed COSMO-MT model on two publicly available datasets. It significantly outperforms existing studies and baseline methods.

title: Diagnosing the Explicit-to-Applied Theory of Mind Gap in LLMs
abstract: As large language models are deployed in high-stakes roles such as therapy, education, and personal assistance, their social cognition must be assessed reliably. Current Theory of Mind (ToM) benchmarks report aggregate scores that conflate two distinct competencies: explicit ToM (recognizing what someone believes) and applied ToM (using that belief to predict behavior). Building on this distinction, we investigate the gap and its recoverability using four structurally diverse benchmarks. Aggregate reporting obscures uneven competence: on SimpleToM, Llama-3.1-8B scores 51.5 percent overall while recognizing mental states at 99.4 percent and predicting behavior at only 28.9 percent. To assess recovery, we compare structured prompting, matched in-context learning, and our proposed Belief-State Test-Time Training (BSTTT), which adapts lightweight parameters on answered support questions through action reconstruction. Across Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, and GPT-oss-20B, recovery depends on the model, task, and intervention. On SimpleToM, reminders combined with BSTTT improve Llama's behavior prediction by 40.8 percentage points; reminders account for most of the overall improvement, with BSTTT adding 1.3 to 5.5 points beyond reminders across models. Contextual examples often outperform weight updates, while BSTTT remains stronger in specific model-benchmark settings. Temporal belief tracking remains difficult despite partial recovery. These findings show that aggregate ToM scores can overstate applied competence while hiding performance recoverable through targeted assistance. We recommend decomposed reporting of explicit and applied accuracy alongside intervention comparisons that establish which failures are recoverable and under what conditions.

title: Directing to Diversify: Multi-Directional Search for Automatic Heuristic Design
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong potential to automate heuristic design for NP-hard combinatorial optimization (CO) tasks without human intervention. Recent methods predominantly rely on evolutionary computation (EC) frameworks, where heuristic diversification is mainly induced through EC-like operators or downstream selection, while the direction of heuristic transformation remains largely unharnessed. In this paper, we propose a multi-directional Perturbation-Rewrite Search (PRS) framework for automatic heuristic design that factorizes heuristic transformation through directional search primitives at the generation level. Specifically, PRS operates on heuristic ideas through three complementary directions: expansion toward richer and more expressive designs, compression toward simpler and less specialized designs, and steering for fine-grained refinement, together enabling broader and more sustained exploration of diverse regions in the heuristic design space. PRS further organizes candidate exploration within a breadth-first search-based process with adaptive operator control, which ensures thorough candidate utilization and sustained exploration, and maintains strong search dynamics while preventing premature convergence. Extensive empirical results across diverse CO tasks show that PRS consistently discovers high-quality heuristics, demonstrating the effectiveness and generality of explicitly directional exploration design.

title: CHATBOT PANDUAN FITUR APLIKASI WAKTOO MENGGUNAKAN TF-IDF DAN SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINE
abstract: Efisiensi layanan karyawan merupakan aspek penting dalam manajemen sumber daya manusia. Namun, keterbatasan jumlah personel sering menghambat penyampaian informasi dan panduan penggunaan aplikasi perusahaan kepada karyawan baru, khususnya mahasiswa magang. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan chatbot sebagai media pendamping dalam memberikan informasi terkait penggunaan aplikasi Waktoo HRM, meliputi presensi, manajemen tugas, dan kebijakan perusahaan. Dataset yang digunakan terdiri atas pattern, response, dan label intent yang disimpan pada database MongoDB. Sistem chatbot dibangun menggunakan Streamlit dengan pendekatan Natural Language Processing (NLP), memanfaatkan Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) sebagai metode ekstraksi fitur dan Support Vector Machine (SVM) melalui implementasi LinearSVC pada pustaka Scikit-Learn sebagai algoritma klasifikasi intent. Evaluasi model dilakukan menggunakan train-test split 80:20 serta Stratified 5-Fold Cross Validation pada data latih untuk mengukur konsistensi dan kemampuan generalisasi model. Kinerja model dievaluasi menggunakan metrik accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, dan confusion matrix. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan accuracy sebesar 84,44%, precision 85,69%, recall 84,44%, dan F1-score 84,01%. Selain itu, cross-validation menghasilkan rata-rata F1-score sebesar 0,87 dengan standar deviasi 0,02 yang menunjukkan performa model yang konsisten. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kombinasi TF-IDF dan SVM efektif dalam mengklasifikasikan intent pengguna pada chatbot Waktoo HRM.

title: Harm Is Behavioural, Moderation Is Lexical: How Language and Culture Decide Whom Automated Safety Systems Protect and Whom They Silence
abstract: Content warning: this paper quotes slurs and hateful statements from published test suites; the racial slur among them is masked. Automated systems decide at scale which messages are harmful, and they decide unevenly. Classifiers label African American English as offensive up to twice as often as other English, the accounts of prominent drag queens can score as more toxic than those of white nationalists, and safety behaviour that holds in English collapses in low-resource languages. We argue that over-flagging and under-protection share one cause: deciding harm from vocabulary and surface form rather than from what a message does. We organise the evidence into seven failure modes and argue, as testable hypotheses, that harmful behaviours (a request for secrecy, a demand for payment, an attempt to isolate someone) travel across languages better than the words that express them. We propose an evaluation protocol that makes the gap between the best- and worst-served language communities a headline result, and show that the naive gap is inflated under equal service and that its usual bootstrap interval is unreliable. Applied to five open systems in eleven languages, from a keyword lexicon to two current multilingual guard models, the protocol finds that none reaches native-speaker accuracy at separating harmful function from harmless form (51 of 55 system-language pairs fall short); that greater capability raises discrimination in nine languages while leaving Arabic and romanised Hindi near chance, so the gap between the best- and worst-served languages grows with capability; that one system both over-flags and under-protects the same language most; and that a language a system reads worst can look the most fairly treated when only false positives are reported.

title: PENGEMBANGAN CHATBOT WHATSAPP BERBASIS DECISION TREE UNTUK OTOMATISASI INFORMASI PENDAFTARAN SANTRI BARU DI PESANTREN
abstract: Digital transformation int he Islamic boarding school environment has prompted the need for a system that can simplify the registration process for new students. This study aims to develop a WhatsApp-based chatbot using the Decision Tree (CART) algorithm as a solution for automating information services and registration forms at the Salafiyah Shirothul Fuqoha Islamic Boarding School Salafiyah Shirothul Fuqoha'. The development method used is a prototyping model with stages of needs analysis, interaction flow design, branching logic implementation, and testing. The chatbot is designed to guide prospective students in accessing information, filling in data, determining dormitoriesbased on program type, and calculating total costs by adjusting to the user's economic conditions. The system was evaluated using a confusion matrix for 25 menu interactions, resulting in an accuracy of 76%, precision of 89.47%, recall of 80.95%, and an F1-score of 85.05%. These results indicate that the Chatbot performs well in accurately responding to structured inputs and is suitable for use in supporting the efficiency of pesantren administration. However, further development is needed in terms of input validation and system scalability.

title: Conflict-Aware Logit Adapters for Utility-Preserving Anti-Distillation
abstract: While reasoning traces improve model capability, they also provide supervision signals for downstream distillation. Initial efforts to mitigate this issue rely on decoding-time interventions, but they incur high inference overhead and can harm the teacher model's natural fluency. We propose Conflict-Aware Logit Adapters (CALA), a lightweight training-time defense. CALA attaches a small residual adapter to a frozen teacher model and trains only the adapter. A proxy student identifies positions where imitation is most sensitive, and the adapter perturbs the output distribution at these positions while remaining within high-probability regions. A conflict-aware optimization strategy balances anti-distillation and utility objectives, while regularization preserves the teacher's performance and fluency. At inference time, CALA incurs modest overhead and requires no auxiliary model. Experiments on reasoning benchmarks show that CALA substantially reduces successful student imitation while maintaining near-original teacher performance and generation quality. These results establish CALA as a practical and efficient alternative to decoding-time approaches.

title: Algorithmic drift in generative adaptive learning
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence promises to democratize personalized tutoring, yet the longitudinal stability of adaptive systems remains under-theorized. Current ethical discourse focuses on static bias. This paper argues that a distinct threat lies in algorithmic drift: a feedback loop in which minor, demographically asymmetric observation errors compound over time into systemic inequities. We make three contributions. First, we formalize algorithmic drift as a coupled learner--tutor dynamical system. Second, we corroborate this theory with an agent-based Monte Carlo simulation in which either a transparent online tracker or an LSTM deep-knowledge-tracing network drives an IRT-based curriculum policy. Third, we introduce the temporal fairness stabilizer (TFS), a targeted intervention that periodically re-probes learner capability, and benchmark it against standard exploration baselines with explicit group-fairness metrics and replication-level inference. Within the modeled environment, TFS closes the achievement gap where generic exploration does not, and we characterize the conditions under which it succeeds. We separate what is established analytically, what is demonstrated in simulation, and what remains to be validated with real learners. Our results reframe algorithmic fairness in education as a temporal property of a closed loop rather than a deployment-time checkbox.

title: ResGVC: Residual Coding for High-fidelity Generative Video Compression
abstract: Generative video compression (GVC) methods usually employ decoder-side diffusion models to denoise reconstructed signals based on generative priors. Besides, most of these methods perform denoising in latent space rather than directly in pixel domain. In this paper, we propose ResGVC, a residual coding framework for GVC that guides denoising toward original pictures by transmitting residual signals. ResGVC first encodes the original pictures within a learned video codec, and then decomposes the distortion between the codec reconstruction and the original pictures into a sequence of residual segments, where each residual segment is acquired at each denoising step. Residual segments can further be compressed by a novel residual codec with a diffusion transformer as an entropy model. Unlike prior methods, ResGVC introduces explicit source constraints throughout denoising rather than relying on decoder-side generation alone. The diffusion-based entropy model also enables more effective distribution modeling capability based on the powerful generative priors. Moreover, denoising directly in pixel space avoids the irreversible information loss caused by latent representation bottlenecks. Experimental results show that, compared with the previous state-of-the-art method, ResGVC achieves 63.7% and 83.8% BD-rate reductions in terms of LPIPS and PSNR, respectively, while also delivering superior visual quality.

title: UPI Fraud Detection Using Machine Learning with AI-Based Risk Score and Transaction Blocking
abstract: The rapid growth of Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions has increased the need for effective methods to detect and prevent digital payment fraud. This project proposes a machine learning-based UPI fraud detection system that analyzes transaction details and identifies patterns that may indicate suspicious activity. Features such as transaction amount, time, frequency, recipient information, device details, and transaction history are used to assess each payment.The system applies machine learning to classify transactions and generate an AI-based risk score. It provides explanations for flagged transactions, such as unusually large payments, repeated transfers within a short period, or payments to unfamiliar recipients. Based on configurable risk thresholds, the system can approve low-risk transactions, send medium-risk transactions for review, and block high-risk transactions. A web-based dashboard displays transaction records, risk scores, alerts, explanations, and decision status for users and administrators.The proposed system aims to support faster fraud monitoring and provide a structured process for handling suspicious payments. Its performance depends on the quality and representativeness of the transaction data used for training and evaluation. The system is intended as a fraud prevention support tool, with final deployment and transaction blocking dependent on integration with authorized payment services

title: Multichoice Modeling: Exploring Decision Configuration Space under Uncertainty
abstract: Decision support has become sophisticated at exploring uncertainty, but much less so at representing the architecture of the decision itself. As a result, the decision space is often narrowed before uncertainty is analyzed, leaving interactions among choices and the effects of alternatives they imply largely invisible. This paper introduces multichoice modeling, a framework for making large decision configuration spaces explicit and computationally explorable under uncertainty. Drawing on the logic of rugged landscapes, we conceptualize such problems as contingent performance landscapes, where interdependent choices generate configuration-specific outcomes whose value changes across uncertain futures. The computational framework combines multidimensional decision and uncertainty spaces in a single simulation. Further, variance-based sensitivity analysis is used for identifying influential choices, and conditional distribution analysis for comparing configuration-specific performance profiles. We demonstrate the framework through three case studies: a manufacturing process upgrade, M&A strategy, and mortgage design. By contrasting conventional uncertainty-only analysis with multichoice modeling, the cases show how opening the decision configuration space can reveal unexpected complementarities, near-best configurations with different risk profiles, and strategies that were not apparent as alternatives at the outset.

title: CANNBot-CAKE: Collaborative Agentic Kernel Evolution for Ascend NPU
abstract: Efficient custom operators are essential for modern deep learning workloads, yet developing high-performance kernels for Ascend NPUs remains slow, expert-intensive, and difficult to automate. Although AI agents now approach expert performance on GPU kernel benchmarks, current models remain less capable of generating AscendC kernels for NPUs, potentially reflecting the relative scarcity of relevant training data. We thus present CAKE, a CANN-native system for deployable custom operators that combines adaptive multi-DSL routing, separate Generation and Evolution modes, and reviewed knowledge reuse through CAKE Book and a Self-Evolving Agent. On 53 CANN-Bench v1.1 operators on Ascend 950PR, CAKE's aggregated results achieve $100\%$ case pass rate on the standard set (1,060/1,060) and $98.28\%$ on the hidden set (4,167/4,240), with an overall mean score of 78.63 out of 100 and an average performance speedup of $1.334\times$ over the baseline. Evolution then pushes correct operators further: EngramGateFusion cuts aggregate device time by $46.6\%$ over 20 rounds and roughly halves the mean roofline gap. These results offer a practical path toward closing Ascend's AI-for-kernel capability gap.

title: Utjecaj generativne umjetne inteligencije na digitalnu autentičnost i povjerenje u online komunikaciji
abstract: Generativna umjetna inteligencija mijenja uvjete u kojima korisnici procjenjuju podrijetlo digitalnih poruka, vjerodostojnost informacija i pouzdanost njihovih pošiljatelja. Cilj je rada kritički razmotriti odnos između sudjelovanja umjetne inteligencije u stvaranju sadržaja, percipirane autentičnosti i povjerenja u online komunikaciji. Primjenjuje se kritički narativni pregled odabranih istraživanja, uz konceptualnu sintezu nalaza o AI autorstvu, označavanju sadržaja i sintetičkim komunikatorima. Razlikuju se empirijski nalazi iz tržišne komunikacije i šire implikacije koje tek treba provjeriti u drugim komunikacijskim okružjima. Analiza pokazuje da se autentičnost ne može svesti na ljudsko podrijetlo poruke, niti se vjerodostojnost može poistovjetiti s njezinom stvarnom točnošću. Negativne reakcije na AI autorstvo ovise o očekivanom ljudskom doprinosu, vrsti poruke i načinu predstavljanja komunikatora. Transparentnost istodobno omogućuje informiranu procjenu i može izazvati nepovoljnije vrednovanje sadržaja. Kao doprinos predlaže se konceptualni okvir provjerljivoga povjerenja koji povezuje podrijetlo sadržaja, obrazloženost tvrdnji, uredničku odgovornost i mogućnost ispravka. Okvir je analitički prijedlog, a ne empirijski potvrđen model. Zaključuje se da odgovorna online komunikacija zahtijeva više od oznake o uporabi umjetne inteligencije: korisniku treba omogućiti procjenu dokaza i utvrđivanje odgovornoga pošiljatelja. Razmatraju se ograničenja postojećih istraživanja te implikacije za informacijsku i AI pismenost.

title: NN-Based Transistor Modeling for Ultra-Fast SPICE Simulation and Standard Cell Library Characterization
abstract: Neural network (NN)-based transistor models have proven to be a promising solution to accelerate device modeling. Although these models demonstrated remarkable speedup in circuit simulations, they were not rigorously tested in complex tasks within standard EDA tool flows for chip design, which require very high transistor model precision to provide accurate results and converge properly. To investigate their full potential and promise, we develop NN-based transistor models that accurately predict the drain current and various charges for a 3nm nanosheet, and employ the models for a standard cell library characterization. This enables us to evaluate the accuracy and speedup under a very wide range of SPICE simulations, benchmarking our models against an industry-standard implementation. Since standard cell library characterization involves thousands of SPICE simulations, it serves as a great benchmark for transistor model quality and consistency. To further evaluate model accuracy, we also perform analog- and digital-level simulations for various complex circuits. Our experiments reveal that NN-based models are a valid alternative to existing transistor compact models, capable of producing accurate delay and power estimates with a much higher speed and convergence time compared to the conventional Verilog-A-based industry-standard (BSIM-CMG) transistor compact model. Our NNs achieve sub-0.11% and 0.76% errors for delay and total power evaluation on a wide range of circuits, while taking up to 8 times less time during the standard cell library characterization. Additionally, we provide comprehensive information and guidance on NN accuracy, unveiling the relationship between NN size and its effect on circuit simulation precision.
